title: 1999 AHSME Problem 20
statement: The sequence \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(a_3,\) \(\ldots\) satisfies \(a_1 = 19,\) \(a_9 = 99,\) and, for all \(n \ge 3,\) \(a_n\) is the arithmetic mean of the first \(n - 1\) terms. Find \(a_2.\)

solutions.text:
For \(n \ge 3,\) \((n - 1)a_n = a_1 + \cdots + a_{n-1}.\) Then \[ a_{n+1} = \dfrac{(n-1)a_n + a_n}{n} = a_n, \] so the sequence is constant from \(a_3\) onward. Hence \(a_3 = a_9 = 99.\)

Since \(a_3 = \dfrac{a_1 + a_2}{2} = \dfrac{19 + a_2}{2} = 99,\) we get \(a_2 = 179.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Show that \(a_n\) is constant for all \(n \ge 3\)
